Action Plan:
1. Suspected anaphylactic/allergic reaction with progressive lip swelling and respiratory symptoms — emergency response initiated: ambulance to be called and patient advised to remain with another person until ambulance/ED arrival.
2. Immediate interim treatment: take any available oral antihistamine now (patient instructed to have accompanying person locate and give antihistamine); administration not documented.
3. If ambulance/ED attend, possible administration of an injection for severe allergy was discussed (type/dose/route not documented).
4. Post-ED follow-up: patient advised to contact the clinic after hospital attendance so clinicians can arrange further management relating to previous severe allergy episodes and "injections" (type/dose not documented).
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: acute onset lip swelling after eating prawn soup.
  - Onset: approximately 30 minutes after eating (around 7:00 PM).
  - Progression: started at left corner of lip, now upper lip swelling increasing in size; patient reports worsening sensation.
  - Associated symptoms: difficulty breathing, sensation of throat closing, generalized breathing difficulty, dizziness.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma (uses salbutamol inhaler regularly; other inhalers denied).
  - History of peanut allergy since childhood.
  - Prior similar episode ~1 year ago with swelling and breathing difficulty after a meal; childhood episode (~age 6) reportedly required an injection/hospital (reported by patient/parent).
- Medications:
  - Salbutamol inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Occasionally takes antihistamines for allergy but specific agent(s) not documented.
- Social history:
  - Initially alone at time of symptom onset; another person (mother) arrived during consult.
- Allergies:
  - Peanut allergy (patient reports).

Objective:
- Patient-reported examination findings:
  - Swelling of upper lip, initially at left corner, now more generalized and increasing.
  - Subjective difficulty breathing and throat tightness.
  - Subjective dizziness.
- No clinician-measured vital signs documented.
- No formal physical examination findings documented by clinician.
- No investigations/results documented.
- Interventions documented in transcript:
  - Clinician recommended ambulance/ED attendance.
  - Clinician instructed to take any available antihistamine immediately.
  - Clinician advised someone present to call emergency services (999).

Assessment & Plan:

1. Suspected anaphylactic reaction:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Suspected anaphylaxis (clinical diagnosis based on acute onset lip swelling, throat tightness, breathing difficulty, dizziness after exposure to prawn).
   - Differential diagnosis: Allergic angioedema (allergic or non-hereditary) — applicable.
   - Investigations planned: Emergency assessment by ambulance/ED (specific investigations not documented).
   - Treatment planned:
     - Emergency transfer to hospital via ambulance (ambulance to be called; patient instructed to remain with accompanying person).
     - Immediate interim administration of oral antihistamine if available (patient instructed to take; administration not documented).
     - Possible administration of an injection for severe allergic reaction (type/dose/route not documented) by emergency services/ED as required (discussed).
   - Referrals: Emergency services/ED (ambulance).

2. Asthma (background):
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: Asthma (history).
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A for background history.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned: Background use of salbutamol inhaler documented (dose/route/frequency not documented). No additional asthma management instructions recorded.
   - Referrals: None documented.

3. Peanut allergy / prior severe allergic reactions:
   - Assessment/likely diagnosis: IgE-mediated food allergy to peanut (patient-reported history).
   - Differential diagnosis: N/A.
   - Investigations planned: None documented in consult; further allergy evaluation may be arranged after ED attendance (patient advised to contact clinic after hospital).
   - Treatment planned: Post-event follow-up to "sort you out" with injections as discussed (type/dose/route not documented).
   - Referrals: Post-ED follow-up with clinic; potential referral/arrangement not specified.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No measured vital signs (pulse, blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, temperature).
  - No documented physical examination by clinician (airway, breathing, circulation, or specific lip/airway assessment).
  - No documentation whether any antihistamine was actually administered.
  - No documentation of whether ambulance was successfully called by clinician or by patient’s accompanying person, or arrival time/status of ambulance.
  - Medication details incomplete: salbutamol dose/strength/frequency not documented; antihistamine agent and dose not documented.
  - No documentation of administration or prescription of intramuscular adrenaline/epinephrine (only discussed as possible).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Clinician first states "I'll call the ambulance" then later instructs the patient's mother to call emergency services (conflict noted regarding who will make the emergency call).
  - Patient uncertainty about prior use of antihistamines and specifics of prior injections (patient reports variable/uncertain history).
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/text intermittently fragmented; some place names and words inaudible or omitted.
  - Patient became acutely unwell during consult with shortness of breath and dizziness, causing some interruptions and reduced clarity.
